notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) HTTP-first sufficed for the whole pass - requests.get with a desktop Chrome UA returned full SSR HTML (~2-2.6MB per page) on every URL tried, no block encountered. robots.txt (checked first) disallows /dashboard/, /order/, /profile/*, /wishlist/, /cart/*, /thankyou/, /order-tracking/, /products/?*, /brands/?*, /collections* (plural) - none of these match the /collection/ (singular) category-page path this site actually uses, and Googlebot gets an explicit blanket Allow, so tier (c) was never needed. DUE DILIGENCE: confirmed this is a real full India storefront, not a thin/redirect shell - it is a Reliance-operated Fynd-platform build of Pottery Barn India (cdn.fynd.com assets) with its own product catalog, ~2.5MB rendered category pages, and a working checkout/order-tracking flow referenced in robots.txt; not a redirect to potterybarn.com. TREE METHOD: sitemap.xml pointed to category_l1/l2/l3 sitemaps which are dummy placeholders (single 'test-l1'/'test-l2'/'test-l3' entry each) - useless. The collections.sitemap.xml (409 URLs) is heavily polluted with SEO landing-page slugs (hundreds of 'dining-table-4-seater' style pages, seasonal/sale/gift/designer-collab collections) so it was NOT used as the source of truth. Instead the real mega-menu nav was pulled directly from the homepage SSR HTML (confirmed identical via a Playwright-rendered pass) and used as the authoritative category tree; the ~150-200 promotional/SEO collection slugs from the sitemap were excluded per rule 27/35 (View All / Collections / Sale / Gift / Designer-collab / SEO-longtail landing pages are not standard nav category/subcategory pages). One nav node (Bedding By Fabric > Sateen) was excluded because its href resolves to a different backend domain (pottery-barn.fynd.io) with a raw filter query string rather than a canonical potterybarn.in collection page - not a valid category URL per rule 29/37. QTY METHOD: each category page embeds its product-listing pagination state as JSON in the SSR HTML; the pattern "item_total":N,"type":"cursor" isolates the true product-listing total (distinguished from an unrelated footer nav item_total that uses "type":"number"). Verified on each leaf that the <title> tag matches the requested node name (catches the bad-slug-silently-serves-parent-total failure mode) before recording qty. EXCLUDED (neither array): Furniture (all of Living Room/Bedroom/Dining/Home Office/Outdoor Furniture, incl. Dressers, Benches & Ottomans, Bookcases & Shelves), Lighting, Mirrors & Art (Wall Art, Wall/Floor Mirrors), Kitchen & Dining Dinnerware/Drinkware & Bar/Serveware/Bestselling Collections (plates, glassware, cake stands, etc - Kitchen & Dining boundary, not Textile/Storage), Cushions & Decor > Candlelight & Home Fragrance, Frames, Planters & Botanicals, Gifts, and Room Decor > Decorative Objects / Vases / Decorative Trays & Bowls (purely decorative, Decorative Home Accessories boundary), Bath > Bathroom Accessories > Countertop Accessories (bathroom fixtures/accessories, not textile or storage). No standalone Storage/Organization/Closet/Laundry/Office-storage nav section exists anywhere on this site - the single storage-qualifying leaf found is Cushions & Decor > Room Decor > Baskets & Storage. Two rows recorded with reduced confidence: 'Robes & Slippers' (Textile, HIGH) - all 3 currently-listed products are cotton bathrobes, no slipper/apparel items populate this qty right now, so primary-product-type test resolves cleanly to Textile despite the ambiguous label; 'Placemats & Chargers' (Textile, LOW, flagged) - site groups textile placemats and non-textile stoneware charger plates under one URL/qty with no way to split them, so per textile.md 22 this is recorded under Textile with a mixed-content flag rather than being forced or dropped. 'Baskets & Storage' (Storage, MEDIUM) - sampled product (Beachcomber Basket) reads as a genuine storage basket per storage.md 5, but basket categories are inherently ambiguous between decorative and storage so MEDIUM rather than HIGH per storage.md 23/42.
